title: Charts & conditional formatting
examples: When should I use a bar chart instead of a line graph?
What is the difference between simple highlighting and conditional formatting?
Can conditional formatting help me spot trends in salary data?

explain.say: Today we are looking at making your data really pop.
Highlighting rules let you automatically change cell colors.
For example, you can make all sales over five thousand green.
When choosing a chart, think about what you want to show.
For instance, if you track website visitors monthly, use a line chart.
A common mistake is using a pie chart for too many categories.

items: Limit pie slices to about five or six.
Too many slices make the chart confusing.
Use a bar chart for many categories instead.

faq.q: When should I use a bar chart versus a line chart?
faq.a: Use a bar chart when you want to compare separate, distinct items. Use a line chart when you want to show how something changes continuously over time.
asks: What's the difference between bar and line graphs?
Should I use bars or a line for sales data?

faq.q: Does conditional formatting work on charts too?
faq.a: Conditional formatting works on the underlying data in the cells, which then drives the chart. You apply the rule to the numbers, not the chart itself.
asks: Can I color the chart based on a rule?
How do I make the chart react to data changes?

faq.q: What is the best chart for showing market share?
faq.a: A pie chart is often used for market share, but it works best when there are only a few major segments. For more accuracy, a stacked bar chart might be better.
asks: Is a pie chart always correct for market share?
What chart shows parts of a whole best?

faq.q: If my data has many categories, what should I use?
faq.a: If you have many categories, a bar chart is usually much clearer than a pie chart. It allows for easier comparison between many items.
asks: Too many items for a pie chart?
What chart handles many data points?

faq.q: Can I highlight based on text, not just numbers?
faq.a: Yes, conditional formatting allows you to set rules based on text content, such as highlighting any cell containing the word 'Urgent'.
asks: Can I format based on words?
Does it work for text criteria?

facts: Bar charts are best for comparing values across different, separate categories.
Line charts are ideal for showing trends or changes over a continuous period, like time.
Conditional formatting applies visual rules (like color) to cells based on their content.
Pie charts should only represent parts that add up to one whole, or one hundred percent.

quiz.say: You are tracking the growth of a company's revenue over the last decade. Which chart type is most appropriate?
quiz.why: A line chart is designed specifically to show continuous change or trends over a period of time.

wrong.0: Scatter plots show the relationship between two different variables, not necessarily a single trend over time.
wrong.2: Bar charts are better for comparing distinct groups, not showing continuous flow.
wrong.3: Pie charts show parts of a whole at a single point in time, not change over years.

quiz.say: You need to show that three departments each contributed a specific percentage to the total company profit. Which chart should you use?
quiz.why: A pie chart is the standard way to visualize how different parts make up a single, total whole.

wrong.0: While similar to a bar chart, the pie chart is specifically meant to show proportions of a total.
wrong.2: A bar chart would imply the departments are separate things, not parts of one whole.
wrong.3: Line charts are for tracking changes over time, which is not the goal here.

quiz.say: You want any cell containing the word 'High Priority' to automatically turn bright red. What feature should you use?
quiz.why: Conditional formatting allows you to set automatic formatting rules based on the text or value inside a cell.

wrong.0: The standard highlighting tool is static and does not react automatically to new data entry.
wrong.2: Manual formatting requires you to remember and click the rule every single time the text appears.
wrong.3: Data validation controls what data can be entered, it does not change the cell's appearance.
